Use finite additivity of `μ.real` together with the three existing measure-real lemmas indicated by the `autoParam` defaults.

- For the first conjunct, write
  \[
  s\triangle t=(s\setminus t)\,\dot\cup\,(t\setminus s).
  \]
  Measurability follows from `hs` and `ht`, and the finiteness assumptions on `μ s` and `μ t` ensure both differences have finite measure. Apply `MeasureTheory.measureReal_symmDiff_eq`.

- For the `Iff`, observe that both universally quantified statements are independently true; no implication between their contents is needed. Establish the finite pairwise-disjoint union formula using `MeasureTheory.measureReal_iUnion_fintype`, and establish
  \[
  \mu.real(s)=0 \iff \mu(s)=0
  \]
  using `MeasureTheory.measureReal_eq_zero_iff`. Then form the equivalence by proving each direction while ignoring its antecedent and invoking the appropriate universal theorem.

The essential mechanism is that `Measure.real` faithfully converts finite `ENNReal` measures to real numbers; the hypotheses excluding `∞` are what make all three identities valid.
